subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should OpenClaw support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk in the bundled OpenAI provider via Gateway relay, and what Azure auth/endpoint contract should be accepted first?
rationale: The remaining work decides how Azure API keys or Entra tokens are stored and used server-side, which endpoint shape is canonical, and what diagnostics or doctor behavior should protect users from leaking credentials or silently falling back to api.openai.com.

options.title: API-key relay first, Entra follow-up
options.body: Ship a provider-owned Gateway relay path for Azure API-key deployments with strict server-side handling, current GA endpoint behavior, Azure-specific diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof, then add Entra once the boundary is proven.

options.title: Require Entra before support
options.body: Hold the feature until Microsoft Entra or managed identity support is designed and tested so the first supported production path is keyless.

options.title: Defer Azure Realtime Talk
options.body: Keep the existing partial bridge unsupported and require users to use direct OpenAI Realtime or an external bridge until Azure model availability and security ownership are clearer.

recommendation.title: API-key relay first, Entra follow-up
recommendation.body: Ship a provider-owned Gateway relay path for Azure API-key deployments with strict server-side handling, current GA endpoint behavior, Azure-specific diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof, then add Entra once the boundary is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They already performed the Azure live-account check and are the clearest owner for deciding whether current Azure availability is enough to sponsor the next proof pass.
